From 67bf002a2d7387a6312138210d0bd06e3cf4879b Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Ruide Cao <caoruide123@gmail.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Apr 2026 12:16:31 +0800
Subject: [PATCH] ipv4: icmp: validate reply type before using icmp_pointers

Extended echo replies use ICMP_EXT_ECHOREPLY as the outbound reply type.
That value is outside the range covered by icmp_pointers[], which only
describes the traditional ICMP types up to NR_ICMP_TYPES.

Avoid consulting icmp_pointers[] for reply types outside that range, and
use array_index_nospec() for the remaining in-range lookup. Normal ICMP
replies keep their existing behavior unchanged.

Fixes: d329ea5bd884 ("icmp: add response to RFC 8335 PROBE messages")
Cc: stable@kernel.org
Reported-by: Yuan Tan <yuantan098@gmail.com>
Reported-by: Yifan Wu <yifanwucs@gmail.com>
Reported-by: Juefei Pu <tomapufckgml@gmail.com>
Reported-by: Xin Liu <bird@lzu.edu.cn>
Signed-off-by: Ruide Cao <caoruide123@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Ren Wei <n05ec@lzu.edu.cn>
Reviewed-by: Simon Horman <horms@kernel.org>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/0dace90c01a5978e829ca741ef684dbd7304ce62.1776628519.git.caoruide123@gmail.com
Signed-off-by: Jakub Kicinski <kuba@kernel.org>

diff --git a/net/ipv4/icmp.c b/net/ipv4/icmp.c
index 2f4fac22d1ab..7eeff658b467 100644
--- a/net/ipv4/icmp.c
+++ b/net/ipv4/icmp.c
@@ -64,6 +64,7 @@
 #include <linux/jiffies.h>
 #include <linux/kernel.h>
 #include <linux/fcntl.h>
+#include <linux/nospec.h>
 #include <linux/socket.h>
 #include <linux/in.h>
 #include <linux/inet.h>
@@ -371,7 +372,9 @@ static int icmp_glue_bits(void *from, char *to, int offset, int len, int odd,
 				      to, len);
 
 	skb->csum = csum_block_add(skb->csum, csum, odd);
-	if (icmp_pointers[icmp_param->data.icmph.type].error)
+	if (icmp_param->data.icmph.type <= NR_ICMP_TYPES &&
+	    icmp_pointers[array_index_nospec(icmp_param->data.icmph.type,
+					     NR_ICMP_TYPES + 1)].error)
 		nf_ct_attach(skb, icmp_param->skb);
 	return 0;
 }
-- 
2.34.1

The patch fixes an out-of-bounds access in the IPv4 ICMP error handling path. The issue arises because extended echo replies use `ICMP_EXT_ECHOREPLY` as the reply type, which is outside the range of the `icmp_pointers[]` array (which only covers traditional ICMP types up to `NR_ICMP_TYPES`). The original code directly indexed `icmp_pointers` without checking the type, leading to potential memory read beyond the array.

### Modifications in each file:

- **`net/ipv4/icmp.c`**:
  - Added `#include <linux/nospec.h>` to use `array_index_nospec()` for speculative execution hardening.
  - In function `icmp_glue_bits()`: Changed the condition that checks `icmp_pointers[icmp_param->data.icmph.type].error`. Now it first verifies `icmp_param->data.icmph.type <= NR_ICMP_TYPES` before accessing `icmp_pointers` via `array_index_nospec(icmp_param->data.icmph.type, NR_ICMP_TYPES + 1)`. This ensures that only valid in-range types are used as indices, while out-of-range types (like extended echo replies) skip the error check entirely.

### Relationship:

The change ensures that the `icmp_pointers` array is only accessed for traditional ICMP types, preventing out-of-bounds reads when handling extended echo replies. The use of `array_index_nospec` also mitigates speculative execution side-channel risks. Normal ICMP behavior remains unchanged.

Here is the commit message:
ipv4: icmp: validate reply type before using icmp_pointers

Extended echo replies use ICMP_EXT_ECHOREPLY as the outbound reply type.
That value is outside the range covered by icmp_pointers[], which only
describes the traditional ICMP types up to NR_ICMP_TYPES.

Avoid consulting icmp_pointers[] for reply types outside that range, and
use array_index_nospec() for the remaining in-range lookup. Normal ICMP
replies keep their existing behavior unchanged.

Fixes: d329ea5bd884 ("icmp: add response to RFC 8335 PROBE messages")
Cc: stable@kernel.org
Reported-by: Yuan Tan <yuantan098@gmail.com>
Reported-by: Yifan Wu <yifanwucs@gmail.com>
Reported-by: Juefei Pu <tomapufckgml@gmail.com>
Reported-by: Xin Liu <bird@lzu.edu.cn>
Signed-off-by: Ruide Cao <caoruide123@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Ren Wei <n05ec@lzu.edu.cn>
Reviewed-by: Simon Horman <horms@kernel.org>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/0dace90c01a5978e829ca741ef684dbd7304ce62.1776628519.git.caoruide123@gmail.com
Signed-off-by: Jakub Kicinski <kuba@kernel.org>

Here is the root cause:
The bug occurs because the `icmp_glue_bits()` function unconditionally indexes the `icmp_pointers[]` array using `icmp_param->data.icmph.type` without checking if the type falls within the valid range (0 to `NR_ICMP_TYPES`). Extended echo replies (ICMP_EXT_ECHOREPLY) have a type value that exceeds `NR_ICMP_TYPES`, leading to an out‑of‑bounds memory read. The root cause is the missing validation on the reply type before the array lookup, combined with `icmp_pointers[]` only being defined for traditional ICMP types.

Here is the patch:
 #include <linux/kernel.h>
 #include <linux/fcntl.h>
+#include <linux/nospec.h>
 #include <linux/socket.h>
 #include <linux/in.h>
  */
 static int icmp_glue_bits(void *from, char *to, int offset, int len, int odd,
 			  struct sk_buff *skb)
 {
 	DEFINE_RAW_FLEX(struct icmp_bxm, icmp_param, replyopts.opt.__data,
 			IP_OPTIONS_DATA_FIXED_SIZE);
 	__wsum csum;
 
 	icmp_param = from;
 
 	csum = skb_copy_and_csum_bits(icmp_param->skb,
 				      icmp_param->offset + offset,
 				      to, len);
 
 	skb->csum = csum_block_add(skb->csum, csum, odd);
-	if (icmp_pointers[icmp_param->data.icmph.type].error)
+	if (icmp_param->data.icmph.type <= NR_ICMP_TYPES &&
+	    icmp_pointers[array_index_nospec(icmp_param->data.icmph.type,
+					     NR_ICMP_TYPES + 1)].error)
 		nf_ct_attach(skb, icmp_param->skb);
 	return 0;
 }

Extended echo replies (`ICMP_EXT_ECHOREPLY`) have a type value that exceeds `NR_ICMP_TYPES`, causing an out‑of‑bounds memory read.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```
#include <linux/nospec.h>
if (icmp_param->data.icmph.type <= NR_ICMP_TYPES &&

```
Reason: The type is first validated to be within the valid range (0 to `NR_ICMP_TYPES` inclusive). Then `array_index_nospec()` is used for the array lookup to prevent speculative out‑of‑bounds accesses. This ensures only legitimate ICMP types are used to index `icmp_pointers[]`, fixing the bug.
